title: MaxRelationship
description: MAXGEN 2.0 -- one family link stored once: a family (a union, household or parent set with its child memberships), one parent and child pair with its lineage facts, or a standing association between two people. Agents never write these files by hand: the helper's link command finds or creates them, and only import_file, resolve_conflict and build_tree tasks may add one directly (R-24). MaxPerson keeps no copy of any link and there is no two-sided lock.

relationship_id.description: This link's permanent id: a random UUID created once by the helper's link command (or by the importer or analysis task that adds it), never computed from the people's ids and never reused.

kind.description: Which of the three kinds of link this document is (family, parent_child or association); each kind forbids the other kinds' fields, and a document of an unknown kind is refused at write and skipped with a warning at read.

is_living_flag.description: Living A floor, required with no default: true when a person this link names may be alive (a family: either partner only, since each child is judged on its own membership; a parent_child record: the parent or the child; an association: either party); unsure means true, it only rises, and the live answer is always computed at read time.

redistribution_license.description: Licence of this link, set by the helper to the strictest of the people it names and the records its claims cite (a family: the partners and the records its family facts cite) and raised later but never lowered; a true is_living_flag requires tier2-private.

media_refs.description: Photographs of the couple or the family, pointing at saved copies that are described once on the records that captured them.

partners.description: Family only: zero to two live partner items, unordered, each either a person or an absent partner whom a document mentions without naming; absent and person items both count toward the two, retracted items stay stored and do not count, and sex is never inferred from a slot.

union_type.description: Family only: the importing program's (or the writer's) word for the kind of union, kept as given, unknown when nothing says; never shown when the family has live family facts, which are the only evidence of a union; shared parenthood alone never makes a marriage.

union_type_as_written.description: Family only: the documents' or the other program's own words for the union, kept when union_type is other or when the words say more.

union_type_uri.description: Family only: a published vocabulary's address for the union type, when one exists.

fact_assertions.description: Family only: facts about the couple or household (marriage, banns, licence, divorce, a census showing them as husband and wife ...), each one claim citing one piece of evidence and held by the partner set.

non_event_assertions.description: Family only: things the evidence says did not happen to this couple (GEDCOM 7 NO), each one claim with the same shape as MaxPerson's; an undated one never counts toward the living test or date bounds.

children.description: Family only: each child's place in this parent set; a child may hold two memberships in one family only when their set kinds differ, because there is one live membership per child, family and set kind (R-20).

parent_id.description: Parent_child only: the parent person, resolved through merge redirects when read; there is exactly one live parent_child record per parent and child pair (R-20).

child_id.description: Parent_child only: the child person, resolved through merge redirects when read; it must differ from parent_id (R-06).

parent_role.description: Parent_child only: the parent's role as the documents show it, unknown until a document says; a later father-versus-mother conflict is refused by the helper for an analysis task to settle.

parent_role_as_written.description: Parent_child only: the parent's own words on the record, such as Head or father, never the child's words.

lineage_assertions.description: Parent_child only: at least one lineage fact saying what kind of parent this person is to this child, each judged on its own evidence; one man who is both birth father and adoptive father has one record holding two facts.

association_type.description: Association only: the kind of standing tie, with this direction: godparent -- party1 is the godparent; enslaved_by -- party1 is the enslaved person and party2 the enslaver; ancestor_descendant -- party1 is the ancestor; employer -- party1 is the employer; neighbour, friend, multiple_birth and other have no direction. Enslavement is never a lineage type, and a godparent named at one rite is a role claim, not an association.

association_type_as_written.description: Association only: the document's or the other program's own words for the tie, kept when association_type is other or when the words say more.

association_type_uri.description: Association only: a published vocabulary's address for the association type, when one exists.

generations.description: Association only, and only with association_type ancestor_descendant: how many generations separate party1 (the ancestor) from party2, when known.

party1.description: Association only: the first party; for a directed type it is the godparent, the enslaved person, the ancestor or the employer.

party2.description: Association only: the second party; for a directed type it is the godchild, the enslaver, the descendant or the employee.

association_assertions.description: Association only: at least one claim that the tie existed, began or ended, each citing one piece of evidence.

partner.description: One partner item in a family: either a person in the tree or an absent partner kept by the document's words without an invented person.

partner_person.description: A partner who is a person in the tree.

person_id.description: The partner person, resolved through merge redirects when read; a partner put in the wrong slot is retracted, never edited.

label_as_written.description: The slot's label as the documents give it (husband, wife, Head, partner); sex is never inferred from it.

label_as_imported.description: The slot's label as another program gave it (such as a RootsMagic spouse, father or mother label), word for word.

family_order.description: This family is the partner's nth union (1 for the first).

family_order_as_imported.description: The other program's own order value for this union (GEDCOM FAMS order, RootsMagic HusbOrder or WifeOrder, Gramps family order), word for word.

outside_ids.description: Another system's ids for this partner link.

notes.description: Notes about this partner in this family (GEDCOM FAMS.NOTE).

extensions.description: Anything another program kept about this partner link that MAXGEN has no field for, under extensions.import.<system>, never dropped.

status.description: Helper-owned: active, or retracted with a reason through retract <family_id>#partner:<person_id>; a retracted item stays stored and does not count toward the two slots.

status_reason.description: Helper-owned: why the item was retracted.

status_task_id.description: Helper-owned: the task under which the item was retracted.

partner_absent.description: A partner whom a document mentions without naming (Mary married in 1850, husband unknown; his widow; GEDCOM 7 HUSB @VOID@ with a PHRASE), kept by its words so that no person is invented.

absent.description: Always true: this slot stands for a partner the documents do not name.

label_as_written.description: The document's own words for the unnamed partner or the slot (husband, his widow).

label_as_imported.description: The slot's label as another program gave it, word for word.

phrase_as_imported.description: The other program's phrase for the unnamed partner (GEDCOM 7 PHRASE under HUSB or WIFE @VOID@), word for word.

extensions.description: Anything another program kept about this unnamed partner that MAXGEN has no field for, never dropped.

status.description: Helper-owned: active, or retracted with a reason through retract <family_id>#partner:absent (also when a named person later fills the slot); a retracted item does not count toward the two slots.

status_reason.description: Helper-owned: why the item was retracted.

status_task_id.description: Helper-owned: the task under which the item was retracted.

membership.description: One child's place in this family's parent set. A membership has no evidence of its own: the evidence lives on the lineage facts of the parent links it uses, or, for a family with no partners, on an existence fact.

membership_id.description: Helper-owned identity key, created once when the membership is first stored and never reused; it is read from input only to match items on a replace.

child_id.description: The child person, resolved through merge redirects when read; a child is never a partner of its own family (R-06).

parent_link_ids.description: The parent_child records this parent set uses, one per parent in the set; it may be empty, and one parent_child record may be used by several memberships.

set_kind.description: What kind of parent set this is for the child: birth, adoptive, a step-family household, foster, guardianship, a church sealing, a competing set not yet settled (alternative_hypothesis) or other; an unknown value is read as other and drawn dotted.

set_kind_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for this parent set, or the helper's words 'kind of parent set not stated' when it had to use other.

child_order.description: The child's place in the family's list of children (1 for the first).

is_preferred.description: Helper-owned: true for exactly one of the child's live memberships, the main parents a chart shows by default; computed by the helper from a recorded preference, else by kind rank and age, never first-come.

preferred_by_task_id.description: Helper-owned: the task under which a preference for this membership was recorded (prefer, a proof's membership_updates, or an importer's prefer); absent when the preference is the computed default.

imported_preferred.description: True when another program called this the child's preferred family (RootsMagic ParentID, FamilySearch preferred parents, the first FAMC); kept as imported, never MAXGEN's own choice.

lineage_as_imported.description: Every lineage word another program gave for this child link (GEDCOM PEDI, Gramps frel and mrel, RootsMagic codes, FamilySearch fact types), word for word.

imported_status.description: The other program's proof status for this child link (GEDCOM 7 FAMC.STAT), word for word; it maps to a claim status only through the import rules.

imported_restriction.description: The other program's privacy restriction on this child link, word for word; a privacy restriction raises is_private.

outside_ids.description: Another system's ids for this child link, such as a FamilySearch child-and-parents relationship id.

is_living_flag.description: Living A floor for this membership, required with no default: true when the child or any parent in it may be alive; unsure means true, it only rises, and a living child raises this flag but never the family's own.

is_private.description: True hides this membership from anything shareable; it only rises (an imported privacy restriction, or the rules for adoptive, foster, guardianship and sealing sets).

status.description: Helper-owned: active; retracted with a reason, never deleted; or merged_away when a merge combined it into another live membership of the same child and set kind.

status_reason.description: Helper-owned: why the membership was retracted or combined.

merged_into_membership_id.description: Helper-owned: the membership this one was combined into by a merge; the unmerge reverses it.

created_at.description: Helper-owned: when the membership was first stored; it orders the computed preference.

task_id.description: The task under which this membership was first stored.

notes.description: Notes about this child link (GEDCOM FAMC.NOTE).

imported_attribution.description: Who the other program says made or changed this child link (FamilySearch ChildAndParentsRelationship attribution), word for word; a credit, never a living flag.

extensions.description: Anything another program kept about this child link that MAXGEN has no field for (such as RootsMagic ChildTable columns), under extensions.import.<system>, never dropped.

lineage_word.description: One lineage word from another program, kept word for word.

system.description: The program the word came from, in lower case (gedcom7, gramps, rootsmagic, familysearch ...).

value_as_written.description: The program's word or code exactly as it gave it (PEDI ADOPTED, Stepchild, 3, AdoptiveParent ...).

parent_person_id.description: The partner the word is about, when the program gives one word per parent (Gramps frel and mrel); a word saying that partner is not the child's parent (Gramps None) gives no parent link for that partner.

partner_as_recorded.description: One partner's own line and age on the cited record.

person_id.description: The partner person this line belongs to.

mention_id.description: The partner's own mention on the record the fact cites, so the privacy check sees every partner's mention.

age_as_written.description: The partner's age exactly as the record gives it.

family_fact_claim.description: One fact about the couple or household, citing one piece of evidence; a civil wedding and a church wedding are two facts in one family, and a remarriage of the same couple is a second family.

fact_type.description: What the evidence says about the couple or household; existence means these people formed a family (a citation of the family as a whole), and a marriage is never inferred from shared parenthood.

fact_type_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for the fact, kept when fact_type is other or when the words say more.

ceremony.description: For a marriage-type fact, the kind of ceremony.

ceremony_as_written.description: The document's own words for the ceremony, kept when ceremony is other or when the words say more.

date.description: When it happened, as the evidence states it.

place.description: Where it happened, as the evidence writes it.

value_as_written.description: A value as written, such as the number of children.

partners_as_recorded.description: Each partner's own line and age on the cited record, so the privacy check sees every partner's mention.

occurrence_id.description: The occasion this fact is about (a MaxEvent id): with document evidence it must equal the cited same-occasion entry's occurrence (the helper fills it when absent) and must be absent when the entry is used indirectly; with other evidence it may name an import or analysis occurrence (section 5.1 of the spec).

non_event_claim.description: One claim that something did not happen (no marriage had happened by a date; GEDCOM 7 NO), the same shape as MaxPerson's non-event claim.

event_type.description: The kind of event that did not happen.

event_type_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for the event type, kept when event_type is other or when the words say more.

date.description: Optional: the period in which it did not happen; an undated non-event is shown as no date given and never counts toward the living test or date bounds.

place.description: Where it did not happen, as the evidence writes it.

lineage_claim.description: One lineage fact: what kind of parent this person is to this child, citing one piece of evidence.

fact_type.description: What kind of parent the evidence shows; a census household line never gives birth_parent (R-17), and an adoptive_parent fact needs the person's recorded yes (R-31).

fact_type_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for this parenthood, kept when fact_type is other or when the words say more.

dimension.description: Which side of parenthood this fact shows; genetic needs evidence basis dna or conclusion (R-18), because a father named on a birth register or certificate is a legal presumption. When it is left out the helper fills a default from fact_type: adoptive_parent and guardian -> legal; step_parent and foster_parent -> household; social_parent -> social; gestational_carrier -> gestational; sealing -> religious; everything else -> unknown.

dimension_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for the dimension, kept when dimension is other or when the words say more.

date.description: When this parenthood began (a birth, an adoption decree, a step-parent's household), as the evidence states it.

end_date.description: When this parenthood ended (a guardianship or fostering that ended), as the evidence states it.

place.description: Where it began, as the evidence writes it.

parent_mention_id.description: The parent's mention on the record the evidence cites.

child_mention_id.description: The child's mention on the record the evidence cites.

amended_record_flag.description: Helper-owned: true when the cited record's record_status is amended, reissued or delayed (R-18), for Quality Control to review; recomputed whenever the cited record is replaced (R-15).

occurrence_id.description: The occasion this fact is tied to (a MaxEvent id), under the same rules as every claim's occurrence_id (section 5.1 of the spec).

association_claim.description: One claim about an association, citing one piece of evidence.

fact_type.description: What the evidence says about the tie: that it existed, when it began, or when it ended.

fact_type_as_written.description: The document's or the other program's own words for this fact, kept when fact_type is other or when the words say more.

date.description: When, as the evidence states it.

place.description: Where, as the evidence writes it.

party.description: One party to an association: exactly one of a person in the tree (person_id) or, for someone not in the tree, their mention on a record (mention, usually with name_as_written).

person_id.description: The party, when they are a person in the tree (resolved through merge redirects when read).

mention.description: The party's mention on a record, when they are not a person in the tree.

record_id.description: The record that names the party.

mention_id.description: The party's mention on that record; a label, never redirected.

name_as_written.description: The party's name exactly as the record or the other program gives it (a GEDCOM 7 @VOID@ associate keeps its PHRASE here).

role.description: The party's role in the tie (godparent, enslaved, enslaver, employer, employee, neighbour, friend ...).

role_as_written.description: The record's or the other program's own words for the party's role.
